Resolves #21508

The taskbar clock spec now measures how far the clock's wait ends from the nearest full minute, on either side, instead of only after it. The clock reads the time a moment after the spec does, so its wait can end a millisecond before the minute and the old remainder wrapped to 59999. The 50 ms tolerance is kept and `src/desktop/Taskbar.mjs` is unchanged. Test-only change; no public behavior changes and no migration.

Evidence: L2 (`Container.spec.mjs`, run locally) -> L2 required (ticket ACs).

## AC Evidence
| AC | Proof |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | The assertion is `Math.min(offset, 60000 - offset) < 50` on `offset = (started + delay) % 60000`. With the clock's wait made 1 ms shorter the spec passes; with it 1 s shorter it fails (`Received: 1000`). |
| AC-2 | `git diff --stat` shows only `test/playwright/unit/desktop/Container.spec.mjs`; the temporary changes to `src/desktop/Taskbar.mjs` for the checks were reverted. |
| AC-3 | `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/desktop/Container.spec.mjs` -> 13 passed. |
| AC-4 | The two checks above: 1 ms shorter passes (13 passed), 1 s shorter fails (1 failed, 12 passed). Not committed. |

## Deltas from ticket
None. The ticket's suggested assertion is used as written, plus a short comment.

## Test Evidence
- `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/desktop/Container.spec.mjs` -> 13 passed locally (Node v22.23.4; the repo asks for >=24, npm warned EBADENGINE only).
- The original flake (a 1 ms read difference landing before the minute) was not reproduced on demand; the 1 ms-shorter check stands in for it.
- Not run: the rest of the unit suite and lint.
